stops.note: from bog 'soft'; peat bog, like the vast Bog of Allen in the Irish midlands, once covered about a sixth of Ireland
taken into English during the Tudor wars in Ireland; bogs preserve 'bog bodies' such as Clonycavan Man, an Iron Age man found in County Meath in 2003

current_meaning: wet, spongy ground of decaying plant matter; (British slang) a toilet
